0.3.0-rc.1.text:
Release candidate 1 of 0.3.0: signed updates and signed install files, a storage reserve, MQTT writes to tagged points only, network fixes and the pre-release hardening.

- Updates are signed by DHC: the unit checks the signature before it downloads anything. Install by file takes DHC's signed release files only (the signature is inside each file); files of older releases are refused. To go back to 0.2.0 by file, use the signed copies slatetap-0.2.0-signed.bin and www-0.2.0-signed.bin from this release.
- Storage: 512 KB stay free so settings, users and alarms can always be saved; trend history shrinks first. System > Storage shows each store against its cap, and a banner warns while memory is low or storage is nearly full.
- MQTT: writes reach only points tagged mqtt-write. BACnet/SC: a warning alarm when no hub has been connected for 10 minutes.
- BACnet/IP: the broadcast table can no longer be rewritten from the network, and foreign devices register only with BBMD and their acceptance on.
- After a Wi-Fi outage, MQTT, BACnet/SC and the fleet heartbeat come back within seconds; a cut web app upload leaves a recovery page, and the unit restores its web app by itself.
- System > Status: an LED legend and a Board card. A firmware file or backup made for another product is refused, with the reason.
- Logic on a phone: a tap on a block opens its settings and help. Deleting a program right after the schedules that wrote its points no longer floods the log.
- An empty access point password left by 0.2.0 becomes the factory default, with a banner until a new one is saved.

0.3.0-beta.5.101.text: Bench test build of signed online updates: each update image carries an ed25519 signature that the unit checks before it downloads anything. Not for sites.

0.3.0-beta.5.text:
Phase E of 0.3.0: the tech tool. An MS/TP analyzer with a capture for Wireshark, a Modbus frame log, OLED alarm and update cards, and a printable commissioning report.

- MS/TP analyzer (System > Support): always on while MS/TP runs. A bus verdict over the last 10 minutes, every station with its timings against the standard limits, and the SlateTap's own pauses counted apart from the bus.
- Capture: record the trunk into memory and download a .pcap for Wireshark; "stop after an error" keeps the frames around an intermittent fault.
- Modbus frame log: what the SlateTap sends on RS485 and what comes back, with the bytes, for 1 to 60 minutes; text and CSV downloads.
- OLED: an Alarms card while an alarm is listed (a new critical or warning alarm takes the screen briefly), an Update card, Updating with its progress during an install, and the bus verdict on the MS/TP card.
- Commissioning report: a printable record of the set-up (Print, or Save as PDF), without passwords, tokens or keys. Every page now prints in a light theme.
- The diagnostics file now carries the analyzer, the capture state and the frame logs.
- RS485: the SlateTap no longer holds the trunk while it saves to flash (its UART keeps working through the write), and after its own pauses it never answers a token the bus has moved past.

0.3.0-beta.4.text:
Phase D of 0.3.0: MQTT, Modbus TCP devices, served BACnet objects, and online updates with release notes, channels and rollback.

- MQTT: points published on change (with a deadband) and in full every few minutes, alarms and status; writes by subscribe reach only points tagged mqtt-write, at a chosen priority and rate limited; Home Assistant discovery (off by default); a site CA for TLS.
- Modbus TCP: up to 8 devices (host, port, unit) on the same point model as Modbus RTU; a device that stops answering goes offline.
- Served objects: every local point is a BACnet object a supervisory system can read; the database revision survives a restart and every object has a description.
- Updates: System > Updates checks the release server (stable or beta channel), shows the notes of every version in between, installs with progress, and rolls back to the other slot. An install window for stable updates is off by default.
- Three crashes within 10 minutes of a restart after an update and the SlateTap goes back to the previous firmware by itself.
- What is new: a card on Home after an update.
- Back on 0.2.0 there is no MQTT and no Modbus TCP: their settings wait unused and return with 0.3.0.

0.3.0-beta.3.text:
Phase C of 0.3.0: schedules, alarm classes, email and webhook notifications, floor-plan pictures and graphic links, a kiosk screen.

- Schedules: a week of events per day, exceptions and holidays (an Ontario list is offered), targets written at a priority, a BACnet object per schedule, and a Schedule block in Logic. Each day starts at the schedule's default value; without the time nothing is written.
- Alarms: classes critical, warning and info (info never rings the bell), acknowledgements that name the user, offline alarms for devices, and the SlateTap's own alarms (clock, storage, memory, certificate).
- Notifications: rules send alarm events by email or to webhooks; undelivered messages wait in a queue that survives a restart.
- Graphics: links between pages, floor-plan pictures converted in the browser, the drawing's source view, five new drawings (make-up air unit, chiller, pump, air handler, floor plan), and a kiosk screen with a QR link.
- Points: tags, favourites on Home, display decimals, bulk changes, and relinquish per priority slot.
- Before going back to 0.2.0, relinquish schedule targets: 0.2.0 leaves their last commands in place.

0.3.0-beta.2.text:
Phase SC of 0.3.0: the BACnet/SC node, SC routing, Network Port and File objects, and standard commissioning.

- BACnet/SC node: TLS 1.3 with mutual authentication to the site's hub, primary and failover hubs, reconnect with a growing backoff, and errors in words (another CA, another name, an expired certificate, a hub that does not trust ours). Connections > BACnet > SC shows the state, the hubs, the certificates and the commissioning steps.
- Routing: SC is a network of the built-in router beside MS/TP and BACnet/IP, so the devices behind a SlateTap are reachable from the SC side.
- Standard commissioning: Network Port objects for every data link, File objects for the certificates (AtomicReadFile, AtomicWriteFile), a key pair and request made on the device, ReinitializeDevice ACTIVATE_CHANGES. Configuration over BACnet is off by default; ReinitializeDevice needs it on and a password (8 to 20 characters, with a lockout).
- More internal memory headroom: with everything on, BACnet/SC connected and an update running, the lowest free internal heap was 102 KB (beta.1: 76 KB).
- BVLC-SC 2-octet fields go out most significant octet first (a patch to bacnet-stack 1.6.1, published in LICENSES/ on the release site).
- Tested against our own hub; not yet against another vendor's.
- Install on 0.2.0 or 0.3.0-beta.1: the firmware image, then the web image. A new or wiped board: the flasher page (merged image).

0.2.0.text:
SlateTap 0.2.0: point-aware Logic, the site database, a BACnet server with router and BBMD, Modbus RTU and TCP, graphics, trends, alarms and the update check.

- Live, point-aware Logic with virtual points and 17 new blocks.
- Site database.
- BACnet server, router and BBMD.
- Modbus RTU and TCP.
- Internet sharing (NAT) and time.
- Graphics, trends and alarms.
- Fleet heartbeat and update check.
- From 0.1.0 by file (Settings > Firmware update): back up first, then the firmware image, then the web app image. Settings, pinned points and programs are kept.
- Not proven yet: the MS/TP side of the router, Modbus RTU on a real wire.
